note: Written from the club directory and Wikipedia only. Nothing about current form, atmosphere or rivalries is included, because none of that is in our data and guessing it would be worse than leaving it out.

alvechurch.text: Alvechurch have been going since 1929, when they started out as Alvechurch Juniors in the Redditch League. The name most people know them for came much later: in 1971 they played out the longest tie in FA Cup history, six games and eleven hours before it was settled. Lye Meadow holds 3,000 and sits about 58 miles from Latimer Park, which makes it one of the longer runs of the season. Worth setting off early for.

anstey-nomads.text: Anstey Nomads were formed in March 1946, when Anstey Methodists and St Mary's merged. They made a real name for themselves in the 1950s with a run of Amateur Cup ties that pulled in record crowds for the village. The Callingtons Community Complex is one of the smaller grounds in the division at around 1,000, and at 29 miles it is one of the closest away days you will get. An easy midweek trip.

banbury-united.text: Banbury United began life in 1931 as the works team of the Spencer Corsets factory, turning professional in 1947. The Spencer Stadium still carries the name. It holds around 2,000 and is 35 miles down the road, which makes this one of the more manageable trips on the calendar and a reliable one for a decent away following.

bishops-stortford.text: Bishop's Stortford were founded at the Chequers Hotel in January 1874, which makes them one of the oldest clubs you will meet this season. Their proudest moment came in 1974, when they became the last winners of the original FA Amateur Cup. Woodside Park is among the bigger grounds in the division at 3,520. It is 52 miles each way, so a proper day out rather than a quick one.

bromsgrove-sporting.text: Bromsgrove Sporting are the youngest club in the division, formed by supporters in 2009 after Bromsgrove Rovers were liquidated. They wasted no time, climbing through three promotions in quick succession. The Victoria Ground is the sort of place that rewards a fan-owned start, holding close to 4,900, one of the largest capacities you will visit. Around 57 miles from Kettering.

bury-town.text: Bury Town date back to 1872, which puts them among the oldest surviving clubs in the country. They play at Ram Meadow in Bury St Edmunds, a 3,500 capacity ground in a lovely part of Suffolk. At 61 miles it is one of the longer eastward trips, so it is worth making a day of the town while you are there.

halesowen-town.text: Halesowen Town, the Yeltz, go back to the 1870s, though the exact year is still argued over. What is not in doubt is the mid 1980s, when they won the FA Vase at Wembley in back to back seasons, 1985 and 1986. The Grove holds around 3,150 and is roughly 60 miles away, out towards the Black Country.

hitchin-town.text: Hitchin Town claim a line back to 1865 and took part in the very first FA Cup in 1871-72, with the current club reformed in 1928. They have played at Top Field throughout, a ground holding around 4,550 that is one of the more atmospheric in the division on its day. Roughly 45 miles from Latimer Park.

leamington.text: Leamington were founded in 1933 as the works team of Lockheed Borg and Beck, and the nickname stuck to the products rather than the place: they have been the Brakes ever since, and were known as AP Leamington through the sponsorship years. The New Windmill Ground holds about 2,300. At 46 miles it is a straightforward enough run over towards Warwickshire.

leighton-town.text: Leighton Town have been going since 1885 and play at Bell Close in Leighton Buzzard, a ground holding around 2,800. They have had a few good runs in the FA Vase over the years, reaching the quarter-finals more than once. At 42 miles this is one of the shorter trips, and a sensible one for a Tuesday night.

leiston.text: Leiston grew out of the Richard Garrett steam engine works and have been going since 1880, with early Suffolk Senior Cup finals in the 1890s and 1900s. Victory Road holds around 2,250. Be warned: at 97 miles this is the longest away day of the entire season, right out on the Suffolk coast. Set off in good time and make a day of it.

needham-market.text: Needham Market as it stands today was established in 1919, though there are records of a club in the town back in the 1890s. Their best day in recent memory came in 2022, when they reached the First Round Proper of the FA Cup for the first time. Bloomfields holds around 4,000, which is generous for the level. It is 75 miles, so one of the bigger journeys.

peterborough-sports.text: Peterborough Sports started out in 1908 as Brotherhoods Engineering Works, and the Turbines nickname still nods to it. They were one of the fastest climbing clubs in the country through the 2010s, with five promotions in seven seasons. Lincoln Road holds around 2,300 and, at 31 miles, this is one of the closest and easiest away days on the list.

racing-club-warwick.text: Racing Club Warwick trace back to 1919 as Saltisford Rovers, taking their present shape in 1970 when Warwick Town and Saltisford Rovers merged. Townsend Meadow is the smallest ground you will visit this season at around 1,280, which tends to make for a closer, noisier afternoon than the capacity suggests. About 45 miles away.

real-bedford.text: Real Bedford were formed in 2002 from a merger of Bedford United and US Valerio, and became one of the most talked about clubs in non-league when podcaster Peter McCormack took over in 2021 with Bitcoin backing and openly stated ambitions of reaching the Football League. McMullen Park holds around 1,000. At 25 miles it is the nearest away trip of the season, so expect a good turnout.

redditch-united.text: Redditch United were formed in 1891 as Redditch Town. The Valley Stadium is the biggest ground in the division at a listed 5,000 capacity, which can make a modest crowd feel a little lost but gives a good away following plenty of room to make some noise. Around 58 miles from Kettering.

rushall-olympic.text: Rushall Olympic have been going since 1893 and reached Step 2 for the first time in 2023, the highest they have climbed. Dales Lane holds around 2,640. At 66 miles it is one of the longer runs of the season, up towards Walsall, so worth sorting travel out in advance.

stamford.text: Stamford were established in 1896 and carry one of the better nicknames in football: the Daniels, after Daniel Lambert, once England's heaviest man, who died in the town in 1809. The Zeeco Stadium holds around 2,000 and at 25 miles this is about as close as away days get. One for a big travelling support.

stourbridge.text: Stourbridge, the Glassboys after the town's cut glass trade, date back to 1876. They have built a reputation as FA Cup giant killers, with Walsall, Northampton and Plymouth among the scalps. The War Memorial Athletic Ground holds around 2,630. It is 64 miles out into the West Midlands, so a longer one.

stratford-town.text: Stratford Town were formed in 1941 as Stratford Rangers, taking the current name in 1949. Their standout day came in 2021, reaching the FA Cup First Round Proper and drawing Shrewsbury Town. The Arden Garages Stadium is on the smaller side at around 1,400. Roughly 52 miles, with Shakespeare's town on the doorstep if you fancy making a weekend of it.

worcester-city.text: Worcester City were established in 1902 and are best remembered for one of the great FA Cup upsets, knocking Liverpool out in 1959. The club has had a difficult time of it in recent years and now plays at Claines Lane, a modest ground of around 1,000 rather than the larger homes of their past. At 72 miles it is one of the longest trips of the season.
